name: Bleached Skull
blurb: A plain, sun-whitened skull, the sort of thing a scholar keeps on a desk to remind him of his own hours.

era.note: An ordinary human skull: memento-mori dressing that ties to no later creature or skill. The art arrived with the 2003 dungeon dressing blocks.

name: Azure Crystal Skull
blurb: A skull carved from a single block of pale blue crystal, so clear that the candlelight seems to live inside it.

era.note: A generic carved crystal skull, a collector's curiosity in any age. Not tied to a creature, race or later skill; the art is later than the era.

name: Jade Tusked Skull
blurb: A green jade skull with two stubby tusks, carved by someone who had seen a great many orcs up close.

era.note: A carved jade skull in the manner of an orc trophy. Orcs existed in the era; the object is a plain curio with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Crimson Crystal Skull Idol
blurb: A blood-red crystal skull in a striped funerary headdress, the kind of idol a tomb robber hopes never to meet again.

era.note: A desert-tomb skull idol in a funerary headdress: generic curse-and-grave-goods dressing, comfortable in any Britannian crypt. Art is post-era.

name: Carved Skull Pedestal
blurb: A skull carved from dark wood and mounted on a stepped pedestal, grave and well made.

era.note: A carved wooden skull bust on a pedestal. Pure dark-magic dressing with no tie to a later skill or monster. Art is post-era.

name: Ember-Eyed Skull Pedestal
blurb: The same carved skull, but with two coals glowing in its sockets that never seem to go out.

era.note: A carved skull bust whose eyes smoulder: ordinary dark-magic theatre, not tied to any later skill, creature or lair. Art is post-era.

name: Skulls on a Pike
blurb: Three stained skulls spitted on a single iron pike, a warning planted where travellers cannot miss it.

era.note: A pike of trophy skulls is generic war and warning dressing; nothing here belongs to a later expansion. Art first appeared in the 2009 Halloween block.

name: Gilded Skeleton Spire
blurb: A gilded skeleton twisted around a spiral spike, grinning at whoever dares to stand close enough to read the warning.

era.note: A golden skeleton on a spike: a generic memento-mori sculpture with no ties to a later creature or skill. Art first appeared in the 2009 Halloween block.

name: Skull Pierced by an Arrow
blurb: A yellowed skull with a black-fletched arrow still buried in the bone, a grim trophy of a good shot.

era.note: A skull with an arrow through it: ordinary battlefield dressing. No creature, skill or lore beyond the era; the art is post-era.

name: Skull Set on a Sword
blurb: A skull set over the grip of a notched blade driven point-first into the ground.

era.note: A skull and sword memorial: generic battlefield dressing that reads naturally in 2000 Britannia. Art is post-era.

name: Skull in a Wreath of Sparks
blurb: A skull haloed by motes of cold blue light, as though some half-finished spell still clings to it.

era.note: A skull wrapped in magical sparks: generic dark-magic dressing, not tied to Necromancy or any other later skill. Art is post-era.

name: Stacked Skull Idol
blurb: Skulls stacked on skulls on a squat stone plinth, with bright red pinpricks glowing in the topmost sockets.

era.note: A stacked-skull totem idol, generic tribal and cursed-shrine dressing. Not a creature figurine and not tied to a later skill. Art is post-era.

name: Skull-Shaped Flask
blurb: A black glass flask blown in the shape of a skull and stoppered with a cork the colour of old bone.

era.note: A glass flask blown in a skull shape: apothecary and sorcerer's-shop curio with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Red Skull Urn
blurb: A tall urn glazed the red of old wine, with a gilded skull set in its belly.

era.note: A glazed urn with a gold skull emblem: ordinary funerary-ware decoration. No later creature, skill or lore. Art is post-era.

name: Skull Incense Burner
blurb: A little wooden boat with a skull at its prow and a stick of incense smouldering at its tail.

era.note: A skull incense burner is ordinary shrine and sorcerer's-parlour dressing with no later lore. The art is post-era.

name: Evil Jester's Mask
blurb: A skull-faced mask under a jester's grey cap and blue bells, grinning in a way that is not at all funny.

era.note: A jester's skull mask is plain carnival and Halloween dressing, tied to no later skill or race. Art first appeared in the 2012 Halloween block.

name: Skull and Spike Cairn
blurb: A heap of skulls pierced through with iron spikes, built up one grim trophy at a time.

era.note: A cairn of skulls and spikes is generic warlord and dungeon dressing. The art first showed in the 2003 dungeon dressing blocks of Malas.

name: Bleached Rib Cage
blurb: The curved ribs of some long-dead traveller, scattered where the dust has half buried them.

era.note: A loose rib cage: ordinary dungeon dressing. The art is original-client art that the main catalog did not use.

name: Bleached Spine
blurb: A long string of knuckled vertebrae, gone the colour of old candle wax.

era.note: A loose spine: plain dungeon dressing from the original art, unused by the main catalog.

name: Scattered Ribs and Femurs
blurb: Ribs and thigh bones strewn about as though something had picked through them and lost interest.

era.note: Plain mixed bones, generic dungeon dressing. Original client art not used by the main catalog.

name: Colossal Spine
blurb: A great arched spine, each vertebra the size of a barrel head, half buried in the dirt.

era.note: A giant beast's spine, generic wilderness bone dressing with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Colossal Rib Cage
blurb: A row of ribs standing in the soil like the gutted frame of a shed, the rest of the beast long gone.

era.note: A giant beast's ribs, generic wilderness bone dressing with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Scatter of Colossal Bones
blurb: Knuckle bones, knobbed ribs and chunks of something big, strewn about where a feast once ended.

era.note: A scatter of giant bones, generic wilderness dressing with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Toppled Skull Totem
blurb: A totem pulled down by someone with a grudge, its skulls now heaped among the broken poles.

era.note: A fallen skull totem, generic war-camp ruin dressing. No later race or lore. Art is post-era.

name: Preserved Heart
blurb: A human heart cured dark and dry, kept by someone with strong opinions about anatomy or about love.

era.note: A preserved heart is ordinary anatomist and sorcerer's-shop dressing. Original client art, unused by the main catalog.

name: Pickled Brain
blurb: A brain the colour of old plums, plucked from a skull and steeped for the benefit of science.

era.note: A preserved brain is ordinary anatomist's dressing. Original client art, unused by the main catalog.

name: Heart on a Wooden Tray
blurb: A preserved heart laid out on a gilt-edged tray, ready for a lesson nobody asked to attend.

era.note: A heart on a tray is plain anatomist's-table dressing. Built from original client tray and organ art; no later lore.

name: Brain on a Pewter Plate
blurb: A pickled brain served on a pewter plate, with an expression that suggests it has had better days.

era.note: A brain on a plate is plain anatomist's or butcher's-joke dressing. Original client plate and organ art; no later lore.

name: Grasping Hand
blurb: A green-grey hand clawing out of the soil, fingers spread for a handhold that is not there.

era.note: A hand clawing from the ground is plain graveyard dressing. Zombies existed in the era; this is a prop, not a creature figurine. Art is post-era.

name: Crimson Ritual Dagger
blurb: A thin, curved dagger with a blood-red grip, the sort of blade that is never used for supper.

era.note: A curved ritual dagger as decor is ordinary dark-magic dressing, tied to no later skill. Art is post-era.

name: Basin of Blood
blurb: A white basin brimming with something thick and dark, with a few drops dried on its rim.

era.note: A basin of blood is ordinary ritual and butcher's dressing. Original client art, not used by the main catalog.

name: Reaper's Scythe
blurb: A long-handled scythe with a notched, rusty blade, said to be favoured by one very patient reaper.

era.note: A scythe as a grim-reaper prop reads naturally in 2000 Britannia (scythes are a farmer's tool). The art was added in 2003 as a weapon icon.

name: Bone-Bladed Scythe
blurb: A scythe whose blade seems to have been grown rather than forged, curved like a rib and pale as one.

era.note: A scythe with a bone blade is generic grim-reaper dressing, comfortable as dark-magic decor. The art dates from 2003.

name: Green-Fire Brazier
blurb: An iron bowl on thorny feet, burning with a tall, pale green flame that gives off no heat at all.

era.note: A brazier burning with magical green fire is generic dark-magic dressing, tied to no later skill or monster. Art is post-era.

name: Black Taper Candelabra
blurb: A tall three-armed candelabrum and its candles, lacquered black from foot to flame.

era.note: A black candelabrum is plain sinister-candle dressing. Original client art, unused by the main catalog; the black hue is from the standard palette.

name: Bloodwax Candelabra
blurb: A table candelabrum with three crimson candles that look suspiciously as if they were poured from something other than wax.

era.note: A red-hued table candelabrum is plain sinister-candle dressing. Original client art, unused by the main catalog.

name: Plague Doctor's Mask
blurb: A long-beaked golden mask of the kind worn by physicians who walked into plague houses so you would not have to.

era.note: A beaked plague mask is a historical physician's costume prop; it ties to no later skill or creature. Art first appeared in the 2011 Halloween block.

name: Daemon Mask
blurb: A horned mask with amber eyes and a scowl, carved to scare small children and the odd tax collector.

era.note: A horned daemon mask is plain festival and ritual dressing. Daemons existed in the era; this is a prop mask, not a creature figurine. Art first appeared in the 2011 Halloween block.

name: Horned Daemon Head
blurb: A great iron-grey horned head with a snarl, mounted so that guests can feel judged from every angle.

era.note: A horned daemon head ornament is generic dark-magic dressing. Daemons existed in the era; this is a mounted trophy prop. Art is post-era.

name: Bronze Daemon Face
blurb: A bronze-coloured daemon face with swept-back horns and a howling mouth, built to ward off the unwelcome.

era.note: A bronze horned daemon face, generic dark-magic dressing. Daemons existed in the era; this is a mounted trophy prop. Art is post-era.

name: Daemon Head on a Platter
blurb: A horned daemon head served up on a bed of leaves with the compliments of a very bold cook.

era.note: A daemon head on a platter is feast-table gallows humour, tied to no later race or skill. Art is post-era.

name: Skull-Marked Grimoire
blurb: A small green book with a silver skull on the cover, the kind that is hidden behind other books.

era.note: A book bearing a skull is ordinary dark-magic dressing and reads as a plain grimoire. Art dates to 2003.

name: Rune-Etched Black Tome
blurb: A squat black book with a plate of strange runes riveted to the cover and no title at all.

era.note: A black tome with a rune plate is generic dark-magic dressing, not tied to a later skill. Art is post-era.

name: Weathered Open Grimoire
blurb: A big weathered book lying open to a page crowded with tiny, anxious handwriting.

era.note: An open weathered tome, generic scholar and sorcerer's-study dressing. Art is post-era.

name: Scattered Skeleton
blurb: Skull, ribs, spine and hip bones strewn across the floor as though the owner had come apart all at once.

era.note: Loose bones arranged into one skeleton: plain dungeon dressing built from original client art that the main catalog skipped.

name: Pyramid of Skulls
blurb: Three skulls for a base and one for a crown, stacked with the tidy pride of a collector.

era.note: A neat pyramid of skulls is classic warlord and ossuary dressing, tied to no later race or skill.

implNote: four-tile composite of one skull graphic

name: Colossal Skeleton
blurb: The whole frame of some great beast laid out where it fell: skull, ribs, spine and mighty thigh bones.

era.note: A giant beast's bones assembled into one skeleton: generic wilderness and dungeon dressing with no later lore. Art is post-era.

implNote: five-tile composite of the giant-bone tiles

name: Anatomist's Table
blurb: A plain plank table with a whole skeleton laid out on it, the day's lecture apparently cut short.

era.note: A skeleton on a plank table is plain anatomist and embalmer's-room dressing. Built from original client art; no later lore.

name: Blood-Stained Stone Slab
blurb: A heavy grey slab slick with something dark, set up where a ritual of the least friendly kind was held.

era.note: A stone slab stained with blood is plain dungeon altar dressing, tied to no later skill or monster. Built from original client art.

name: Blood-Stained Table
blurb: A rough plank table with a great dark stain across the top, and nobody keen to explain it.

era.note: A bloodied plank table is plain butcher and dungeon dressing. Built from original client art; no later lore.

name: Memento Mori Candelabra
blurb: A gilt candelabrum burning over a quiet skull, set out to remind the reader how little time there is.

era.note: A skull beneath a candelabrum is a classic memento-mori study piece, with no tie to a later skill or monster.

name: Bloodstone Crystal Skull
blurb: A skull cut from deep red crystal, with a dark core that looks too much like a swallowed ember.

era.note: A red-hued carved crystal skull, a generic collector's curiosity. Not tied to any creature, race or later skill; the art is post-era.

name: Amber Crystal Skull
blurb: A skull of clear amber-gold crystal, lit from within like honey held up to a lamp.

era.note: An amber-hued carved crystal skull, a generic collector's curiosity with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Silvered Skull Pedestal
blurb: The carved skull on its stepped pedestal, rubbed to a pale, silvery finish.

era.note: A carved skull bust in a silvered finish; ordinary dark-magic dressing with no tie to a later skill. Art is post-era.

name: Obsidian Skull Pedestal
blurb: The carved skull on its stepped pedestal, finished glossy black like a piece of cut obsidian.

era.note: A carved skull bust in a black finish; ordinary dark-magic dressing with no later tie. Art is post-era.

name: Alabaster Skull Idol
blurb: A stacked-skull idol rubbed to the pale colour of alabaster, grim but oddly serene.

era.note: A stacked-skull idol in a pale finish: generic tribal shrine dressing with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Obsidian Skull Idol
blurb: A stacked-skull idol finished black as pitch, the red glints in its sockets all but gone out.

era.note: A stacked-skull idol in a black finish: generic cursed-shrine dressing with no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Silver Skull Urn
blurb: A tall urn glazed in pale silver, with a skull set in its belly like a seal.

era.note: A glazed funerary urn with a skull emblem in a silver tint: plain funerary-ware dressing, no later lore. Art is post-era.

name: Black Skull Urn
blurb: A mourning-black urn with a skull in its belly, kept by families who do not much like to talk about it.

era.note: A glazed funerary urn with a skull emblem in black: plain funerary-ware dressing, no later lore. Art is post-era.
